key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Sudden, abrupt start. LOCATION: Chest (palpitations), generalized symptoms. DURATION: Sustained (>30 seconds) or non-sustained bursts. CHARACTER: Rapid, regular or slightly irregular palpitations. AGGRAVATING: Exertion, electrolyte abnormalities. RELIEVING: Cardioversion, antiarrhythmics. TIMING: Can be episodic or sustained. SEVERITY: Variable, can be asymptomatic to severe symptoms. KEY POSITIVES: Heart rate 120-250 bpm, wide QRS on electrocardiogram (ECG), history of myocardial infarction (MI) or cardiomyopathy, syncope, chest pain, dyspnea, altered mental status. KEY NEGATIVES: NOT narrow complex tachycardia (SVT).

red_flags: History of myocardial infarction (MI) or cardiomyopathy
History of sudden cardiac death in family
Pulselessness (V-Tach with no pulse = ventricular fibrillation )
